{"code": "import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Create a side-by-side comparison of response rates by sex and treatment
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: Response rate by sex
response_by_sex.plot(kind='bar', ax=axes[0], color=['skyblue', 'salmon'])
axes[0].set_title('Response Rate by Sex (Overall)')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Proportion Responded')
axes[0].set_ylim(0, 1)

# Add value labels
for p in axes[0].patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    axes[0].annotate(f'{height:.3f}', (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
                     ha='center', va='bottom', xytext=(0, 3), textcoords='offset points')

# Plot 2: Response rate by treatment
response_by_treatment.plot(kind='bar', ax=axes[1], color=['lightgreen', 'lightcoral'])
axes[1].set_title('Response Rate by Treatment')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Proportion Responded')
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 1)

# Add value labels
for p in axes[1].patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    axes[1].annotate(f'{height:.3f}', (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
                     ha='center', va='bottom', xytext=(0, 3), textcoords='offset points')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/output/fig_response_rates.png')
plt.close()

# Print summary of key findings
print('Summary of key findings:')
print(f'1. Overall, women have a higher response rate (0.694) than men (0.679).')
print(f'2. The control group has a higher response rate (0.720) than the treatment group (0.631).')
print(f'3. The treatment group has balanced sex distribution (160 F, 160 M).')
print(f'4. The control group has more men than women (276 M, 252 F).')
print(f'5. Within the control group, women respond better (0.758) than men (0.685).')
print(f'6. Within the treatment group, men respond better (0.669) than women (0.594).')"}
